title: SAP's ECC deadline is 2027. Around half of DSAG's ECC users expect to run past it.
metaTitle: SAP ECC 2027: why DSAG members are pushing back
description: 54% of DSAG companies still run SAP ECC or Business Suite. Around half of DSAG's ECC users expect to run past 2027.
dek: SAP's German-speaking user group wants customers to set their own path. There's no Australian survey like it that I've seen, but ERP partners here will recognise the mood.
author: Shane Kennedy

shortVersion: 54% of companies in DSAG's investment survey still run SAP ECC or Business Suite. Standard maintenance for ECC runs out at the end of 2027.
Around half of DSAG's ECC users expect to run past that, onto extended support at a 2% premium until the end of 2030.
DSAG's outgoing chairman told more than 6,000 people that companies running SAP should set their own course. I'd expect the partners customers trust to win the ECC work.

beats.heading: Where DSAG's members stand
body: DSAG is the German-speaking SAP user group, covering Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Its investment survey from early 2026 found 54% of companies still use SAP ECC or Business Suite.
Standard maintenance for ECC runs out at the end of 2027. For many of those companies, that means a move to S/4HANA. It's expensive, Hungershausen said. And the business benefit often isn't clear.

graphic.label: of DSAG companies still run SAP ECC or Business Suite

beats.heading: The pushback
body: At DSAG's annual congress in October, outgoing chairman Jens Hungershausen told more than 6,000 people that companies running SAP should set their own course and their own pace, and make well-founded decisions.
Cloud's the future, he said. But for many members, S/4HANA on-premise and hybrid systems are what's running today.

graphic.text: S/4HANA On-Premise and hybrid architectures are the everyday reality for many of our members, and SAP has to accept that.

beats.heading: The ECC clock
body: A DSAG survey of 198 senior leaders, run between December and January, suggests around half of its ECC users will run past the 2027 deadline. There's extended support until the end of 2030, at a 2% premium.

Hungershausen says that doesn't mean those firms will sit and wait until 2030. "They simply need this time due to the complexity of their system landscapes," he said, pointing to skills shortages, parallel projects and limited budgets.

graphic.eyebrow: The ECC clock for DSAG members

beats.heading: AI, built elsewhere
body: DSAG's investment survey also asked about AI. In January, 43% of respondents had AI use cases in place, and the vast majority weren't built on SAP's tools.
Hungershausen said companies are "simply doing a better job of providing easy access to AI".

graphic.label: had AI use cases in place in January

beats.heading: What it means for ERP partners here
body: That's Europe. I haven't seen an Australian survey like it, but ERP partners here will recognise the mood. Customers who haven't moved don't want to be rushed, and they want an honest path forward.
Let's say a customer on ECC asks whether to move now or use extended support. A useful answer depends on their systems, their budget and their people. That's much the same list Hungershausen gave.

graphic.label: No comparable survey I've seen here

body: The partners who win that work will be the ones customers trust to tell them what makes sense for their business, deadline or not.

sources.title: SAP customers seek renewed control over their ERP fate
Half of German-speaking SAP users set to blow past 2027 ECC support deadline

notes: These are German-speaking SAP users (Germany, Austria and Switzerland), not Australian ones.

The 54% and 43% come from DSAG's investment survey, as reported by CIO.com. The "around half" comes from a DSAG survey of 198 senior leaders run from 8 December 2025 to 21 January 2026, as reported by The Register. They may be the same survey.
Reports differ on how many ECC users plan to switch by the end of 2027, so this post doesn't use that figure.
"What it means for ERP partners here" and "Shane's take" are my opinion, not DSAG's.
